newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS-HK stocks expected to face further selling.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-HK stocks expected to face further selling.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks have embarked on a slippery path which could take prices lower in the short term until earnings reports revive investor interest in the market, strategists said on Thursday.
"The market ran very strongly in December and January running up to Chinese New Year," said Pauline Gately, regional strategist at Merrill Lynch.
"Without a new stream of earnings upgrades or news from China, I think that we really have run our course in the short term," she said.
The Hang Seng Index took a tumble on Thursday, sliding 222.66 points, or 1.65 percent, to 13,239.95. The fall brought losses this week to 420.55 points, or 3.08 percent.
Concerns about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping have spread jitters in the market over recent days, brokers said.
"I think that those rumours will ebb and flow and could have some temporary impact on the market," said Gately.
But analysts said the effects would not last.

"Ultimately Deng does not factor into the equation anymore in terms of China's relationship with Hong Kong. It is more of a symbolic event," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
Strategists said investors were really looking at valuations in the Hong Kong market. The Hang Seng Index hit an all-time high on January 16 at 14,004.93 points.
"It got a bit overvalued between December and early January and people are likely to be taking profits," said Marshall Mays, chief strategist at Nikko Research Center (Hong Kong).
"I would not be surprised to see it go below 13,000. I think it is a pretty easy bet."
Gately said the blue-chip index could even fall to 12,800 points before resuming its uptrend. "I would be happier to see a bit more consolidation," she said.
Mays said investors were raising cash and also looking at markets like the Philippines, Singapore and Malaysia.

Morgan Stanley regional strategist Peter Churchouse said he had become more "favourably disposed" towards the Malaysian market recently and may raise its weighting in Morgan Stanley's Asia-Pacific (non-Japan) model portfolio.

"Basically I think the Malaysian market has the capacity to suprise investors again this year. I think there are some very good economic, macro fundamental reasons why Malaysia is looking reasonably attractive," he said.
Churchouse said Hong Kong stocks could consolidate over the next month or two, but he remained positive on a 12-month view.

"I still believe that the market will be a front-runner in the region in 1997," Gately said. "I think that if the index pulls back to the levels I am talking about then that would be an opportunity to commit further funds."
She said economic news coming out of China should be positive and the interest rate environment should remain benign.
"We have got year-end (company) reports coming out this month. That will likely give a little lift to the market," Mays said.
